must_remember: Ferromagnetism originates from the quantum mechanical exchange interaction that couples adjacent electron spins.
Above the Curie temperature ($T_C$), a ferromagnetic substance transforms into a paramagnetic substance obeying the Curie-Weiss law $\chi = \frac{C}{T - T_C}$.
Magnetic hysteresis represents the lag of magnetic induction ($B$) behind the magnetizing field ($H$) during a full cycle.
Retentivity is the residual magnetism when $H = 0$, while coercivity is the reverse field required to reduce $B$ to zero.
The Weiss molecular field approximation expresses the internal effective field as $B_m = \lambda M$.

glossary.meaning: A quantum mechanical electrostatic interaction that aligns adjacent electron spins parallel or antiparallel.
The critical temperature above which a ferromagnetic material loses spontaneous magnetization and becomes paramagnetic.
The ability of a material to retain residual magnetization when the external magnetizing field is removed.
The magnitude of the reverse magnetic field needed to bring residual magnetic induction down to zero.
An effective internal magnetic field assumed by Weiss to align atomic dipoles in ferromagnets, proportional to magnetization.
